LESSON: WRITING 5.3.1 WRITING SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we connect ideas in sentences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension
2. construct sentences using different language structures to give information
3. appreciate using sentences for effective communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 5.3.1 WRITING SENTENCES
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 5.3.1 WRITING SENTENCES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Construct sentences using different language structures to give information

What this means
In this part you learn to construct sentences using different language structures to give information. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: construct sentences using different language structures to give information.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can construct sentences using different language structures to give information. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate using sentences for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate using sentences for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate using sentences for effective communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate using sentences for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences to a partner. (skill: construct sentences using different language structures to give information)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate using sentences for effective communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension.
3. Practise this skill: construct sentences using different language structures to give information.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate using sentences for effective communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we connect ideas in sentences?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 5.3.1 Writing Sentences means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify parts that make a sentence for comprehension.
5. Be able to: construct sentences using different language structures to give information.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
